triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: “What Æsop?” the President asked sternly again. “Oh, Pierrot ... my father, Fyodor Pavlovitch.”

triples.subject: Dmitri
triples.quote: Grigory’s description of the scene at the dinner-table, when Dmitri had burst in and beaten his father, threatening to come back to kill him, made a sinister impression on the court

triples.subject: Dmitri
triples.quote: He observed that he was not angry with Mitya for having knocked him down and struck him on the face; he had forgiven him long ago, he said.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: he still persisted that the arrangement with the son was “unfair,” and that he ought “to have paid him several thousand roubles more.”

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: related how Smerdyakov had once found the master’s money in the yard, and, instead of concealing it, had taken it to his master, who had rewarded him with a “gold piece” for it

triples.subject: Captain Snegiryov
triples.quote: Ilusha, my little son. ‘Father, father, how he insulted you!’ He said that at the stone. Now he is dying....

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: On being asked about Mitya’s attack upon him, he refused to answer. “God bless him. Ilusha told me not to. God will make it up to me yonder.”

triples.subject: Rakitin
triples.quote: When, after Rakitin’s cross-examination, the President asked the prisoner if he had anything to say, Mitya cried loudly: “Since I’ve been arrested, he has borrowed money from me!
